sentences.text: The claimants, being dissatisfied with compensation of Rs.15,56,800/- awarded to them by the Tribunal in respect of an undisputed accident, which took the life of Sahayakumara, 51 year old, are in appeal.
2. The contention of the claimants is that the deceased was running a barber shop apart from his agricultural activities.

The claimants contented that he was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month and in support of this contention, they produced two lease agreements which indicated that the deceased was paying a sum of Rs.4,500/- per month as rent to the shop that he had taken on rent for running his business.
The claimants also produced the bank passbook of the deceased to show regular remittances of cash into his account.

A perusal of these documents, according to me, justify the contention of the claimants that deceased was earning more than Rs.11,000/-, which is determined by the Karnataka State NC: 2024:KHC:50747 Legal Services Authority as notional income for persons, who are not able to establish the income with adequate evidence.

entities.text: Karnataka State NC: 2024:KHC:50747 Legal Services Authority
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, I am of the view that it would be appropriate to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.13,000/- instead of Rs.12,000/- determined by the Tribunal.
3. Since the deceased was aged 51 years and was self- employed, 10% requires to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.14,300/-.
If 1/4th is deducted towards personal expenses, his monthly income would be Rs.10,725/-.

The income of the deceased for the purposes of determining the 'loss of dependency' would thus be Rs.10,725/-.
4.
As the deceased was aged 51 years, a multiplier of '11' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.14,15,700/- (Rs.10,725/- x 12 x 11) towards "loss of dependency".

The claimants being the wife, children and mother, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/- towards "loss of consortium" i.e., in all Rs.2,90,400/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.36,300/- under the "conventional heads".

6. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums:

 1. Loss of Dependency 14,15,700

Thus, the claimant would be entitled to compensation of Rs.17,42,400/- as against Rs.15,56,800/-
awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest from the date of petition till its realization.
8. The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

10. Out of this compensation amount, only the sums awarded towards 'love and affection' be dispersed to the children and mother of the deceased and the entire enhanced compensation shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of claimant No.1-wife, for a period of five years.
11. This appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
